title: Nimbus Retail — interactive SLO heuristics and burst characterization (field lab notes)
body:
Purpose:
Run a short field lab to validate heuristics for interactive SLOs on a retail customer workload ("flash-checkout" modal with product recommendations). Goal: determine practical knobs to keep p95 < 120ms for single-round chat-style queries while minimizing cost uplift during short microbursts (5–30s).

Background/context:
Nimbus runs an in-product recommendation modal triggered on checkout. Traffic profile is low steady QPS (~12 qps) with frequent microbursts up to ~600 qps for 10–25s (marketing rushes). Model choices: open-7B quantized (A100/4x), distilled-3B (CPU fallback), and a small reranker (600M) for final ranking. Customer requires: interactive feel, p95 target 120ms on hosted slot, cost budget target <= 1.8x baseline CPU-only rerank cost.

Test setup (field lab VM mix):
- Serving runtime: latest internal lab build (rt-v0.12.3) with prefix KV-cache and adaptive batching enabled.
- Model variants: open-7b-q4_0 (primary), distill-3b-fp16 (fallback), rerank-600m-int8 (reranker).
- Cluster: 4x A100-80GB (dedicated pool), 2x NVLink groups for KV-sharing experiment, 3x c6i-type fronting proxies for connection handling.
- Configs tested:
  * B0: default batching (max_batch=64, max_latency_ms=40), kv_cache disabled
  * B1: adaptive batching (max_batch=128, dynamic latency target 30ms), kv_cache enabled with LRU expiry 300s
  * B2: aggressive batching (max_batch=256, max_latency_ms=100), kv_cache enabled, prefetch warmup sequence on model load
- Traffic generator: replayed traces from Nimbus production week of 2026-09-22 with synthetic microbursts (shape: base 12 qps, compound bursts to 600 qps for 10–25s every 6–9min).

Observed metrics (representative runs):
- B0 (no cache): steady p95 = 140–170ms, burst p95 spike = 450–950ms, tokens/sec per GPU = 220–280, observed cost factor ≈ 2.1x baseline.
- B1 (adaptive + kv): steady p95 = 95–110ms, burst p95 = 180–250ms (95th during peak windows only), tokens/sec per GPU = 320–380, cost factor ≈ 1.6x baseline.
- B2 (aggressive batch + prefetch): steady p95 = 110–130ms, burst p95 = 140–200ms, tokens/sec per GPU = 420–480, cost factor ≈ 1.9x baseline.

Key observations / interpretation:
- KV-prefix cache is the single biggest win for interactive retail flows where many requests share prompt prefixes (product title + user context). Enabling kv reduced steady p95 by ~35–40% in our runs and reduced compute by lowering effective token work.
- Adaptive batching (B1) gave the best balance: it preserved low steady-state latency and limited tail amplification during short bursts by reducing batch formation time when queues jump.
- Aggressive batching (B2) raises steady latency slightly but smooths burst tails; good for throughput-focused SLAs but borderline for the customer's interactive constraint.
- Warmup/prefetch sequences (issue: showed benefit when used within 60s of expected burst but cost is incurred continuously if left enabled). A hybrid approach (on-demand prefetch triggered by traffic detection) was promising in microtests.
- Fallback to distill-3b during sustained overloads preserved p99 but produced a small semantic regression — requires product review.

Quantitative tail breakdown (B1 run, representative):
- steady window (10k requests sampled): p50=34ms, p90=78ms, p95=103ms, p99=198ms
- microburst window (spike to 600 qps, 20s window): p50=58ms, p90=160ms, p95=212ms, p99=810ms
- cold-starts (after 5 min idle, first 20 requests): p95=420–650ms (warmup sequence reduced cold p95 by ~60%)

Cost notes (rough):
- Baseline (small rerank CPU-only): $0.48 / 1k requests (customer baseline for comparison)
- B1 effective blended cost: ~$0.85 / 1k requests (~1.77x baseline)
- B2 effective blended cost: ~$0.92 / 1k requests (~1.92x baseline)
- Notes: cost includes reserved GPU pool amortization in the POC (not final pricing).

Practical heuristics we validated for Nimbus: (these should be translated into Redwood Optimize recipes)
1) Enable prefix KV-cache with per-customer LRU TTL 300s for conversational-ish retail prompts.
2) Use adaptive batching with a low dynamic latency target (25–35ms) for interactive SLOs.
3) Implement an event-driven prefetch: warm the model when ephemeral upstream signals indicate an impending burst (promo webhook / CDN edge metrics).
4) Route by priority: critical checkout flows get primary model lanes; best-effort recommendations can be routed to distilled model when queue depth exceeds threshold X (empirically X ~ 120 requests queued across pool).
5) Keep a small always-on GPU pool for fast responses (1–2 GPUs) and allow autoscale bursts to larger pools for throughput efficiency.

Open questions / risks:
- Product tolerance for degradation when falling back to distill-3b is unknown; need A/B trial with UX team.
- Prefetch triggers: who owns the upstream signal? If customer cannot send webhooks we need to rely on noisy heuristics (edge latencies) which risk false warms.
- Cost model: POC amortization hides some infra cold costs — finance should model committed vs. burst pricing for final proposal.
- Security/compliance: KV cache stores prefixes — ensure no PII persists in cache TTL window or add scrub step.

Action items / next steps:
- [Priya] Draft a short one-pager for Nimbus product (2 slides) explaining tradeoffs and recommended B1 baseline (due 2026-11-05).
- [Ethan] Prototype event-driven prefetch using CDN-edge webhook (proof-of-concept in SE-4123 branch, due 2026-11-12).
- [Miguel] Run a 48h soak under B1 with real replay schedule and full pricing calc (start 2026-11-08).
- [Lina] Coordinate UX A/B for fallback quality check with Nimbus PM (sync by 2026-11-10).

Notes to self / rough heuristics that may go into Optimize catalog:
- If >60% of requests share first 40 tokens, enable prefix caching by default.
- Dynamic latency target of 30ms yields best steady/burst compromise for sub-200ms p95 targets.
- For microbursts <30s prefer adaptive batching; for sustained high QPS (>2 minutes) shift to higher bs and model consolidation.

Appendix: quick run commands (lab reproducibility)
- Traffic replay: python tools/replay.py --trace gs://redwood-pocs/nimbus/2026-09-22.trace --scale 1.2 --burst-overlay bursts.json
- Start pool: scripts/lab_start_pool --profile open-7b-q4_0 --count 4 --kv-ttl 300 --adaptive-batching true
- Measure: go run tools/collector/main.go --tags nimbus-b1 --out results/b1-2026-10-14.json

End of notes.

Unresolved: need a short live demo script that shows B1 vs B0 side-by-side (customer asks for visual). Priya to prepare quick dashboard snapshots for next customer call.
summary: Field lab notes for Nimbus retail interactive SLO heuristics. Adaptive batching + KV-prefix cache (B1) provided best balance: p95 < 120ms steady-state and contained burst tails to ~200ms in most microbursts while keeping cost under the 1.8x budget. Several operational heuristics and next steps listed.
